identity.description: Amazon Selling Partner API (SP-API): Amazon's REST API for sellers and vendors to manage Amazon marketplace data and operations, documented at developer-docs.amazon.com/sp-api.
identity.identity_notes: Search results from developer-docs.amazon.com and sell.amazon.com both describe the Selling Partner API as Amazon's seller/vendor API. Direct fetches of developer-docs.amazon.com/sp-api returned a 301 to a malformed host (developer-docs.amazon/, no TLD), which I did not follow, so identity rests on search-result excerpts and the sell.amazon.com developer page.

auth.oauth_flows: Authorization-code OAuth 2.0 flow built on Login with Amazon (LWA). The selling partner grants consent via the Appstore or an Authorize button on the developer's website; the app exchanges the authorization code for a refresh token.
auth.token_refresh: Refresh token is exchanged at the LWA token endpoint (api.amazon.com/auth/o2/token) for an access token, which expires one hour after issue (per search-result excerpt of the authorization docs). Authorization code expires after five minutes.
auth.scopes_notes: Not established from fetched pages. Scope/role details were not retrieved.

access.production_restrictions: Developer profile is reviewed by Amazon; the decision to grant SP-API access is based on the developer profile information. Public apps listed in the Selling Partner Appstore require a complete security review. Sandbox registration does not need to wait for profile approval. Sources conflict on whether a Professional selling account is required: the sell.amazon.com page and the registration docs say yes; a FAQ says a Professional account is not needed for sandbox endpoints.

api.limitations: Sandbox returns static mock responses for most APIs; a dynamic sandbox exists for select APIs (per search excerpt). Resource breadth was not verified from fetched vendor pages, so it is left Unknown.

claims.value: Amazon Selling Partner API is documented under developer-docs.amazon.com/sp-api and the Selling Partner API is Amazon's seller API
Authorization is an OAuth 2.0 flow built on Login with Amazon (LWA)
LWA access token expires one hour after issue; refresh token used at api.amazon.com/auth/o2/token
Amazon decides whether to grant SP-API access based on the developer profile information
Sandbox application can be registered while the developer profile is under review
Sources conflict on whether a Professional selling account is needed for the developer profile vs. sandbox
claims.quote: No, you don't need a Professional Selling Account to develop or integrate with Sandbox endpoints.
claims.verify_note: quote not found in fetched source text

claims.value: Notifications API delivers to SQS or EventBridge destinations rather than HTTP webhooks
amzn/selling-partner-api-samples contains a Local MCP for SP-API developer tools and a Data Kiosk MCP server
claims.quote: This repository contains sample code in various programming languages for use cases supported by the Amazon Selling Partner API (SP-API).

claims.value: Sample solutions are not supported products in their own right
claims.quote: These sample solutions are not supported products in their own right, but educational examples

open_questions: Exact resource breadth (orders, catalog, listings, inventory, reports, feeds, finances, etc.) was not verified from vendor pages; breadth left Unknown.
Whether a Professional selling account is required to create the developer profile is contradictory across Amazon sources; tier set to paid_plan provisionally.
Official SDKs (e.g., amzn GitHub SDK repos) were not verified; sdks left unknown.
Rate limits per endpoint were not retrieved.

Whether the Data Kiosk MCP server in amzn/selling-partner-api-samples accesses live seller data was not established.
Scopes/roles for private vs public apps were not established.
Whether the community repos are maintained was not checked.
